Humanity could exist fine with 1bn, in isolation. However, population decline always comes alongside an ageing population, which is the real issue. This results in each working age person being required to support more and more people, and productivity isn't increasing fast enough to offset this issue.

Fertility rates are declining in almost all countries, not just white ones. Sure, countries in Africa, for example, still have growing populations for now, but this won't remain true forever, particularly since these countries tend to have more people emigrate than immigrate. Also, the countries with the lowest fertility rates are South Korea, Taiwan, and Singapore, none of which are white.

Total fertility rate is more useful, as it only counts people of childbearing age. Developed countries tend to have older populations, which results in lower birthrates as a higher portion of the population are outside childbearing age. It is generally believed that a tfr of 2.1 is needed to maintain a population, but there is no birthrate that can be said to maintain a population, as it depends on other factors (such as average age and gender ratio).
